annotationStatus: Editorial casting interpretations based on the existing source-backed character summaries. Metaphors and cautions are design guidance, not canonical abilities or verified BOTC compatibility.

ahsoka-tano: Her separation from the Jedi institution makes independence distinct from disloyalty. Her mentoring and protective role suggest personal judgement exercised outside official authority.
Independent investigation, mentorship and protecting another player.
Independence does not imply unreliable information.
asajj-ventress: Betrayal by her former master changes the meaning of her allegiance. Revenge, survival and self-direction provide a more specific portrait than simply treating every former Sith associate as evil.
Changing allegiance, surviving betrayal and retaliation.
Choose a life stage; allegiance changes over time.
bb-8: A mobile companion carrying a particular clue, rather than an all-knowing investigator. Loyalty and initiative make information delivery and protecting a message stronger associations than abstract wisdom.
Carrying a clue, communicating limited information and supporting a partner.
Possessing one clue is not universal knowledge.
bo-katan-kryze: Her identity combines a warrior's direct action with the responsibility of reclaiming a homeland. Leadership here concerns legitimacy, collective loyalty and the consequences of pursuing power.
Public leadership, contested authority and reclaiming a position.
Leadership alone does not justify any powerful ability.
boba-fett: A hunter whose reputation and survival shape how others perceive him, later associated with holding territory and authority. The distinction between pursuing a target and governing a community matters when casting.
Pursuit, reputation, survival and a transition into authority.
Select hunter or ruler rather than mixing both indiscriminately.
c-3po: A protocol specialist whose knowledge is expressed through communication and interpretation. His partnership with R2-D2 makes complementary information roles more natural than independent supernatural insight.
Translation, interpreting a message and communicating information.
Communication expertise is not truth detection or omniscience.
cad-bane: A dangerous professional pursuing high-risk targets. Investigation serves a hunter's objective, while deception and survival support calculated interference rather than communal truth-seeking.
Tracking targets, precise disruption and escaping consequences.
A hunter's investigation need not align with the good team.
cassian-andor: An intelligence operative associated with secrecy and sacrifice. His narrative function concerns gaining actionable information while concealing his work, with costs attached to serving a wider cause.
Covert intelligence, concealed allegiance and sacrificing personal safety.
Secrecy does not automatically make a role deceptive or evil.
chewbacca: A warrior and copilot whose strongest casting distinction is dependable partnership. Protection, friendship and endurance point toward helping another person rather than directing an entire political system.
Protecting a partner, enduring danger and loyal support.
Physical strength is not immunity to every kind of harm.
count-dooku: His move from Jedi to Sith and leadership of the Separatists combine changed allegiance with visible political authority. Manipulation works through organisation and influence, not merely personal aggression.
Political manipulation, changed allegiance and directing other agents.
A fallen Jedi is not evidence for every alignment-changing mechanic.
darius-pax: The League's founder recruits a challenger to an established champion. His documented role is organisational: creating an arena for rivalry and seeking an intervention in its power structure.
Recruiting an agent and shaping who participates in a contest.
Game details remain limited to cited official announcements.
darth-maul: Survival after defeat and the creation of a criminal power base distinguish him from a generic Sith aggressor. Revenge gives continued action a personal objective even after former authority is lost.
Returning after defeat, revenge and building an alternative power base.
Surviving defeat does not mean unrestricted resurrection.
darth-vader: The Anakin/Vader identity makes transformation, concealed history and conflicting loyalties central. His casting can emphasise oppressive power or redemption, but those are different points in his story.
Changed identity, corruption, coercion and costly redemption.
Choose a life stage before interpreting his alignment.
din-djarin: A bounty hunter whose relationship with Grogu foregrounds protection over detached pursuit. A concealed presentation and a personal duty suggest selective guardianship rather than general command of others.
Protecting a chosen person and balancing duty against personal loyalty.
Armour and secrecy do not imply invulnerability or false registration.
emperor-palpatine: His concealed Sith identity and acquisition of public political authority create a specific double presentation. Manipulation and control operate through apparently legitimate influence, making hidden responsibility more relevant than brute force alone.
False public presentation, hidden control and corrupting others.
Political deception is not an explanation for unrelated information abilities.
ezra-bridger: An orphan becoming a trained Jedi combines learning, initiative and a developing relationship with dangerous power. His confrontation with the Empire supports personal growth and sacrifice rather than an already infallible mentor.
Developing insight, temptation and sacrificing personal freedom for others.
Intuition does not guarantee accurate information.
finn: A former stormtrooper becoming a Resistance ally makes chosen loyalty more important than inherited position. His change of side distinguishes redemption and new commitments from ongoing sabotage within a hostile organisation.
Leaving an allegiance, changing sides and protecting new allies.
Defection is a story transition, not proof of arbitrary team switching.
general-grievous: A cyborg commander of droid forces whose menace centres on military pressure and intimidation. His ability to direct organised violence is a different metaphor from subtle social manipulation or secret information gathering.
Coordinated attacks, intimidation and directing destructive agents.
Military danger alone does not explain poisoning or misinformation.
grand-admiral-thrawn: Studying opponents and their cultures turns observation into strategic control. His distinctive casting strength is inference from evidence about an enemy, rather than instinctive prophecy or random information.
Reading patterns, identifying an opponent and planning around observed behaviour.
Strategic inference can be mistaken; it is not magical certainty.
grand-moff-tarkin: Command of the Death Star associates public authority with overwhelming threatened consequences. Control here is institutional and coercive: others must account for the cost of resisting his position.
Public coercion, severe consequences and authority over destructive power.
Threatened destruction is not a substitute for a role-specific mechanism.
grogu: A young Force-sensitive survivor under another character's protection combines vulnerability with latent power. The relationship between dependent and guardian is more distinctive than treating Force sensitivity as generic information access.
A vulnerable protected person with occasional consequential intervention.
Limited known control over power should not become omniscience.
han-solo: A smuggler joining the rebellion combines opportunism with growing commitment. Improvisation, risky choices and loyalty to companions give him a different casting purpose from a disciplined investigator or political leader.
Risk-taking, improvisation and helping a partner despite personal cost.
Recklessness alone does not make him a fool or unreliable investigator.
hera-syndulla: The Ghost crew's pilot and leader combines operational initiative with responsibility for companions. Her casting is strongest when leadership coordinates or protects a group, rather than when it merely signifies status.
Coordinating allies, protecting a crew and supporting a shared mission.
Command does not imply controlling another person's allegiance.
hibi: A mechanic preparing and upgrading Shade's vehicles supports another person's performance. Knowledge is practical and technical, expressed through improvements and preparation rather than discovering hidden identities.
Improving another participant's effectiveness through technical support.
Vehicle upgrades do not establish canonical healing or resurrection powers.
jabba-the-hutt: A crime lord holding Han captive combines territorial influence, greed and control over a particular victim. The clearest casting angles involve leverage, confinement and deals backed by intimidation.
Holding leverage over a target and making coercive bargains.
Criminal authority does not mean knowledge of every secret.
jar-jar-binks: A participant in Naboo's affairs who later represents his people politically. The contrast between initiative and unintended consequences supports well-meant intervention that can reshape a situation beyond its original purpose.
Unintended consequences and a public intervention with a larger cost.
Comic presentation is not evidence of stupidity or inaccurate information.
jyn-erso: Her connection to Galen and participation in stealing the Death Star plans join personal history to a decisive collective mission. Initiative, hope and sacrifice centre on securing something others can use.
Obtaining vital information through personal risk and sacrifice.
Delivering a plan does not imply recurring nightly investigation.
kanan-jarrus: A Jedi survivor mentoring Ezra while serving with a rebel crew. Concealed history, instruction and protection offer complementary casting angles: passing on knowledge and accepting danger for someone less experienced.
Mentoring a learner, protecting another person and concealed identity.
A hidden background is not automatically false alignment registration.
kestar-bool: An established champion using status to intimidate competitors and expand influence. His rivalry with Shade anchors power in a contest with identifiable opponents, rather than a vague claim of general villainy.
Suppressing a rival, exploiting status and controlling a competitive arena.
Official pre-release material does not establish additional secret abilities.
kylo-ren: The Ben Solo/Kylo Ren distinction foregrounds identity, inner conflict and allegiance shaped by corruption. Power and possible redemption should be tied to a chosen story period rather than flattened into a permanent moral label.
Conflicted allegiance, identity change and costly redemption.
Specify a life stage; internal conflict is not random information.
lando-calrissian: His administration of Cloud City and dealings with Vader precede his rebel allegiance. Conflicting obligations, compromised choices and recovery of trust offer a particular metaphor for deals made under pressure.
Compromised bargains, divided obligations and recovering loyalty.
Distinguish coercion from freely chosen betrayal.
leia-organa: A princess, rebel leader and Resistance founder whose authority is tied to organising resistance. Loyalty, judgement and protection are expressed through responsibility for a cause and its people, not just prominence.
Public leadership, organising allies and protecting a collective cause.
Being a leader does not explain every powerful Townsfolk ability.
luke-skywalker: A farm boy becoming a Jedi and confronting his father connects developing insight with hope for another person's redemption. The strongest casting angles involve learning, refusing a destructive path and taking risks to preserve someone.
Learning, resisting corruption and helping another person change direction.
Hope and intuition are not proof of guaranteed truthful information.
luthen-rael: An antiquities dealer with a concealed role coordinating resistance. The divide between public occupation and private purpose supports hidden organisation, manipulation and the costs of keeping a cause alive.
A concealed coordinator directing other people behind a public identity.
A covert good cause need not map to an evil team.
mace-windu: A senior Council member associated with judgement and confronting Palpatine. His narrative role combines institutional responsibility with a decisive assessment of danger, rather than indiscriminate force or detached prophecy.
Judging a threat, exercising authority and committing to decisive action.
Sound judgement is not immunity to deception.
moff-gideon: An Imperial remnant leader pursuing Grogu for secret research. Control and hidden knowledge serve a focused exploitative project, making targeted capture and use of another person's capabilities stronger casting angles than generic evil.
Targeted exploitation, secret research and controlling a valuable subject.
Research does not give access to every ability in the script.
mon-mothma: A senator becoming a rebellion and New Republic leader combines political influence with concealed commitments. Her casting can distinguish patient coalition-building and responsibility for others from direct combat intervention.
Concealed political work, coalition-building and collective leadership.
Political secrecy does not imply misinformation or evil allegiance.
obi-wan-kenobi: Training Anakin and later watching over Luke join mentorship with long-term protection. Loyalty, concealed presence and sacrifice suggest a guardian carrying knowledge while allowing another person to take the central role.
Mentoring, protecting a specific person and preserving a concealed history.
Knowledge carried by a mentor is not omniscience.
padme-amidala: A queen and senator with a secret marriage combines visible political responsibility with private loyalties. Those two spheres make diplomacy, concealed relationships and conflicting obligations more distinctive than a generic benevolent leader.
Public diplomacy, a private relationship and divided obligations.
A secret relationship does not establish false team registration.
poe-dameron: A Resistance pilot whose initiative and loyalty sit alongside recklessness and leadership. His casting should distinguish bold operational choices from reliable deduction: taking charge is not the same as correctly identifying another person's alignment.
Bold action, risky initiative and responsibility for allies.
Recklessness alone does not justify Village Idiot's alignment information.
qui-gon-jinn: An independent-minded teacher discovering Anakin emphasises judgement outside institutional consensus. Intuition and mentorship suggest recognising potential and acting on a conviction, while accepting consequences for that choice.
Recognising potential, selecting a learner and following independent judgement.
Intuition about potential is not infallible identity detection.
r2-d2: An astromech carrying important information across several generations of heroes. Knowledge is stored and delivered, while initiative and protection concern accomplishing a task despite danger rather than debating it publicly.
Preserving a secret, delivering information and practical intervention.
Stored information differs from freely learning a new fact every night.
rex: A clone officer serving with Anakin and Ahsoka before aiding the rebellion. Loyalty is therefore a considered relationship rather than unconditional obedience, with leadership and protection expressed through commitment to companions.
Questioning inherited allegiance, protecting allies and leading a group.
A clone identity does not justify duplicating any arbitrary BOTC role.
rey: A scavenger becoming a Jedi combines resourcefulness, developing insight and questions of identity. Hope and protection support an emerging hero's choices, while concealed history should remain distinct from deliberate deception.
Discovering identity, developing insight and resisting a corrupting legacy.
Unknown origins do not mean she deliberately gives false information.
sabine-wren: An artist and demolitions specialist in the Ghost crew combines creativity with practical sabotage. Intervention is deliberate and technical, giving clearer casting possibilities than merely associating colourful presentation with unpredictability.
Creative intervention, targeted sabotage and changing a practical situation.
Technical sabotage does not establish supernatural poisoning.
sebulba: A competitive podracer whose interference targets opponents in a shared contest. His Galactic Racer connection adds conditional support for Shade, so hostile rivalry and potentially useful patronage should be treated as different contexts.
Sabotaging a rival, interfering with performance and conditional support.
Do not invent a confirmed vehicle or unrevealed Galactic Racer ability.
shade: A mysterious challenger recruited against Kestar Bool, with a grudge against the Bool family. Secrecy, initiative and revenge frame a personal rivalry, while Hibi's technical support links him to an identifiable helper.
A concealed personal objective, challenging a rival and relying on support.
His mystery is not evidence for an unrevealed secret identity or power.
supreme-leader-snoke: A First Order leader training Kylo Ren and linked to Palpatine's schemes. His casting centres on corrupting influence and an ambiguous position within another controller's plans, rather than assuming every visible leader is the ultimate source of power.
Corrupting a learner and exercising control within a larger hidden scheme.
Avoid treating visible authority as proof of independent ultimate control.
yoda: A long-serving teacher continuing to train Luke while in exile. Wisdom, perception and mentorship make guidance and interpreting limited evidence useful metaphors, with the distinction between teaching and directly solving a mystery retained.
Mentorship, guidance and interpreting signs rather than direct intervention.
Wisdom does not make every piece of information guaranteed true.
